 Redmi K100 launches in China on Oct. 27; the iQOO Neo 12 follows on Oct. 28, both at 7 p.m.
 The K100 has a 10,000mAh battery, 11% bigger than the Neo 12's confirmed 9,000mAh cell.
 The Neo 12 runs the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, up to 19% faster in single-core than the K100's chip.
 Only the iQOO has a built-in fan: a 59-blade unit with three speeds and a 15% better vapor chamber.
 K100 is tipped at about $523 (CNY 3,500); the Neo 12 has no price yet, and that number decides the winner.
 The Redmi K100 vs iQOO Neo 12 matchup comes down to one trade. Redmi gives you a 10,000mAh battery and a power-saving gaming chip on top of 2024’s Snapdragon 8 Elite. iQOO counters with the newer Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 , a sharper 2K screen, and a built-in cooling fan , but 1,000mAh less battery.
 Timing makes this comparison unusually tight. Redmi launches the K100 in China on October 27 at 7 p.m., and iQOO follows with the Neo 12 exactly 24 hours later , on sale right after the event. If you don’t follow these brands: Redmi is Xiaomi’s value line, and iQOO is Vivo’s performance line, and both sell flagship-level speed for roughly half of flagship prices. Neither phone is in stores yet, so this comparison runs on official teasers, clearly labeled leaks, and our own math across eight rounds .
 Best Choice XIAOMI Redmi Note 15 
   5/5 Overview 
 AMOLED display delivers sharp details and vivid colors
 High-resolution camera captures detailed everyday photographs
 Large battery supports extended daily smartphone usage
 CHECK PRICE See latest price on Amazon
 Price and Availability: One Tipped Price, One Blank 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 China launch Oct. 27, 7 p.m. Oct. 28, 7 p.m. (on sale immediately) 
 Starting price Tipped ~$523 (CNY 3,500) Not announced 
 Last year’s model K90: $388 (CNY 2,599) Neo 11: $388 (CNY 2,599) 
 Global plans None announced None announced 
 Tipster Digital Chat Station claims the K100 will start at around CNY 3,500 . That’s only $30 below the K100 Pro’s $553 (CNY 3,699) , and the Pro has the newer chip. If the tip holds, the K100 costs 35% more than the K90 did at launch, with the same main processor.
 iQOO hasn’t shared any pricing. Its Neo 11 started at $388 (CNY 2,599) last year, but memory prices have pushed nearly every Android brand higher in 2026. So here’s how we’d read the Neo 12’s price when it lands. These are our hypotheticals, not leaks.
 If the Neo 12 starts at… Our take 
 CNY 2,999 (~$448) Easy pick for most gamers: newer chip, fan, 2K screen, and $75 under the tipped K100 
 CNY 3,299 (~$493) Still the stronger all-rounder; the K100 makes sense only if battery is your top priority 
 CNY 3,499 (~$523) A true toss-up between battery and speed 
 CNY 3,699+ (~$553+) The K100 Pro becomes a better comparison than either 
 Outside China, both are uncertain. Xiaomi often sells Redmi K phones abroad as Poco models, sometimes with smaller batteries. Tipster Debayan Roy claims a version of the Neo 12 could reach India as the iQOO 16R, though another leak trail ties that name to a different phone.
 No winner until iQOO’s price is public on October 28. 
 Design: Fan Vent vs Water Resistance 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 Frame Metal (reported) Metal 
 Back Firefly Green shown Shifting-light “Zhengfeng” finish; extra color co-developed with the China Academy of Art 
 Camera module Two lenses (based on teasers) Square module with a circular fan vent 
 Water and dust IP68 (reported) Not announced 
 Weight and thickness Not announced Not announced 
 Neither brand has shared weight or thickness yet, which matters a lot here. A 10,000mAh battery and a built-in fan both take up space, so expect both phones to be on the heavier side.
 The bigger difference is protection. The K100 is reported to carry IP68 , which means it should survive dust and a dunk in fresh water. iQOO hasn’t confirmed a rating for the Neo 12, and a phone with a fan has a vent that lets air in and out. iQOO says the fan uses a double-layer waterproofed circuit board, but that isn’t the same as an official rating.
 Redmi wins narrowly, until iQOO confirms an IP rating. 
 Display: iQOO Is Sharper and Faster 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 Size 6.83″ Not confirmed 
 Resolution 1.5K 2K 
 Max refresh rate 165Hz 185Hz 
 Time per frame at max 6.1 ms 5.4 ms 
 Brightness (as quoted) 3,500 nits peak 2,200 nits 
 Instant touch sampling 3,500Hz 5,000Hz 
 Multi-finger touch sampling 480Hz 500Hz 
 Native high-frame-rate games 40+ at 165fps 50+ at 185fps 
 Refresh rate is how many times per second the screen redraws. At their peaks, the Neo 12 shows about 12% more frames per second, which works out to a 0.7-millisecond difference per frame. Very few players can feel that, and very few games run anywhere near 185fps without help from a gaming chip.
 Resolution is the more visible upgrade. A 2K panel packs in more pixels than 1.5K, so text and in-game details look sharper.
 The K100’s 3,500 nits looks far brighter, but be careful. Redmi quotes a peak figure, usually measured on a small bright patch, while iQOO’s figure has been described as full-screen. They aren’t measured the same way, so brightness stays unscored until reviews test both. Touch sampling , how often the screen checks for your finger, also edges to iQOO, which helps in fast shooters.
 iQOO wins this round. 
 Performance: A Newer Chip Beats an Extra Helper 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 Main chip Snapdragon 8 Elite (late 2024) Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 (late 2025) 
 Geekbench single-core ~3,031* 3,621 
 Geekbench multi-core ~9,829* 11,078 
 Gaming helper chip D2 Q3 
 Memory (leaked/reported) 12GB LPDDR5X, 256GB UFS 4.1 16GB 
 *Score from a Galaxy S25 Ultra, which runs the same Snapdragon 8 Elite. The K100 hasn’t appeared on Geekbench yet.
 Geekbench is a benchmark app that measures processor speed. Single-core reflects quick tasks like opening apps, and multi-core reflects heavy work like exporting video. The iQOO Neo 12 ‘s Geekbench listing puts it about 19% ahead in single-core and 13% ahead in multi-core, compared with what a Snapdragon 8 Elite phone like the Galaxy S25 Ultra scored. Different phones and firmware, so treat that as a rough guide.
 Here’s a detail that says a lot about the K100’s position: iQOO already sold the Snapdragon 8 Elite last year. The iQOO Neo 11 launched in October 2025 with that exact chip. So in 2026, Redmi is shipping the processor iQOO moved on from a year ago.
 Both phones add a second, smaller helper chip for games, and both do two jobs:
 Upscaling: The game renders at a lower resolution, and the helper chip sharpens it to full resolution, so the main chip works less.
 Frame generation: The helper chip invents in-between frames, so a game running at 72fps can look like 144fps.
 Redmi pitches the D2 on efficiency. It claims an average 1.1W power saving in Honor of Kings at 144fps on max settings. iQOO pitches the Q3 on ceiling, promising 2K at 185fps plus full-scene ray tracing, a lighting technique that makes reflections and shadows look more realistic. One catch for both: generated frames can add a tiny delay between your tap and the screen, so competitive players often switch them off.
 For today’s games, the Snapdragon 8 Elite is still plenty. The gap shows up two or three years from now, as games get heavier.
 iQOO wins this round. 
 Cooling: A Real Fan vs a Smarter Workload 
 This is the clearest hardware difference between the two phones.
 The Neo 12 has a built-in cooling fan , part of what iQOO calls its Ice Dome system. Official teasers say the fan has 59 blades and three speed levels , and it works alongside a vapor chamber, a thin sealed plate of liquid that spreads heat away from the chip. iQOO says that the vapor chamber moves heat 15% better than the Neo 11’s.
 The K100 has no fan. Redmi’s approach is to make the main chip work less in the first place, by handing upscaling and frame generation to the D2.
 Why does it matter? Phone chips slow themselves down when they get hot, a process called thermal throttling . A fan pushes heat out of the body, so frame rates stay closer to their peak in long sessions. It’s the same reason more brands say gaming phones need fans for 2nm chips .
 The trade-off is a moving part, a vent, and some noise. Redmi’s approach has none of those, but it can only reduce heat, not remove it.
 iQOO wins this round. 
 Cameras: Too Early to Call 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 Main 50MP Light Hunter 800, 1/1.55″, f/1.68 (official) 50MP with OIS (tipster claim) 
 Ultrawide Likely (second lens in teasers) 8MP (tipster claim) 
 Telephoto None None expected 
 Redmi has confirmed a 50MP Light Hunter 800 main sensor. Sensor size matters because bigger sensors collect more light, which helps at night. iQOO hasn’t announced the Neo 12’s cameras. Tipster Debayan Roy claims a 50MP main camera with OIS , short for optical image stabilization, which physically steadies the lens against shaky hands, plus an 8MP ultrawide .
 Neither phone is built for photography, and neither has a zoom lens. If photos matter more to you than frame rates, the Xiaomi 18 with two 200MP cameras is a better fit than either.
 No winner until iQOO confirms its cameras. 
 Battery and Charging: Redmi’s Whole Argument 
 Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 
 Capacity 10,000mAh 9,000mAh 
 Energy density Not announced 916Wh/L 
 Wired charging 100W (reported, not official) 100W (official) 
 Last year’s model K90: 7,100mAh Neo 11: 7,500mAh 
 Year-over-year jump +41% +20% 
 The K100 carries the biggest battery Redmi has ever shipped, 11% more than the Neo 12. Both use silicon-carbon cells, also called silicon-anode batteries, which mix silicon into the part of the battery that stores charge so it holds more energy without getting bigger.
 The year-over-year jump tells you where each brand put its budget. Redmi grew its battery by 41%. iQOO grew its battery by 20% and spent the rest on the chip and the fan.
 Capacity isn’t the same as battery life. Newer chips usually finish the same task using less power, and a fan that keeps the chip cooler can help too, because hot chips waste more energy. Until reviewers run the same tests on both, Redmi’s 11% lead is a lead on paper. At the tipped price, it works out to about $52 per 1,000mAh .
 Redmi wins this round. 
 Software and Extras: Two China-First Skins 
 The K100 ships with HyperOS 4 on Android 17. Its headline feature is Super XiaoAi 2.0, Xiaomi’s voice assistant, now running on Xiaomi’s own MiMo large language model, the kind of AI behind chatbots. Redmi also adds Bose-tuned dual speakers and a large X-axis vibration motor for sharper haptic feedback.
 The Neo 12 is reported to run OriginOS 7 on Android 17, based on its Geekbench listing. iQOO has confirmed a 3D ultrasonic fingerprint reader , which uses sound waves to map your fingerprint and works better with wet fingers than optical readers. Leaks say the K100 gets an ultrasonic reader too.
 Both software skins come loaded with China-specific apps, and we haven’t seen either brand commit to a specific number of Android updates for these phones yet.
 Call it a draw. 
 The Phone Both of Them Should Worry About 
 There’s a third option sitting just above both: the Redmi K100 Pro , already on sale in China at $553 (CNY 3,699) .
 Redmi K100 Redmi K100 Pro iQOO Neo 12 
 Chip Snapdragon 8 Elite Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 
 Battery 10,000mAh 8,580mAh 9,000mAh 
 Cooling fan No No Yes 
 China price Tipped CNY 3,500 CNY 3,699 Not announced 
 If the K100’s tipped price is right, $30 more gets you Redmi’s newer chip in the K100 Pro, at the cost of about 14% less battery. That’s why the K100 only works if battery life really is your top priority, and why iQOO’s price matters so much: anything at or below CNY 3,499 puts the Neo 12’s newer chip and fan below both Redmis.
 So, Which One Should You Buy? 
 We compared official teasers, certification-based reports, benchmark listings, and tipster claims. Neither phone has been reviewed yet.
 Round Redmi K100 iQOO Neo 12 Our pick 
 Price and availability Tipped CNY 3,500 Not announced Too early 
 Design IP68 (reported) Fan vent, no IP rating yet Redmi, narrowly 
 Display 1.5K, 165Hz 2K, 185Hz iQOO 
 Performance Snapdragon 8 Elite + D2 Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 + Q3 iQOO 
 Cooling No fan 59-blade fan iQOO 
 Cameras 50MP official Not announced Too early 
 Battery and charging 10,000mAh 9,000mAh Redmi 
 Software and extras HyperOS 4, Bose speakers OriginOS 7, ultrasonic reader Draw 
 Final tally: iQOO 3, Redmi 2, one draw, two rounds still open. 
 Get the Redmi K100 if you want a phone that gets through heavy days with charge left over, you play casual games more than competitive ones, you want IP68 water resistance, or you’d rather not have a fan and a vent in your phone.
 Get the iQOO Neo 12 if you play for an hour or more at a time, you play competitive shooters where touch response and native frame rates matter, you want the sharper 2K screen, or you plan to keep the phone for three years or more and want the newer chip.
 Best Overall OnePlus 15 
   5/5 Overview 
 6.78 inches, LTPO AMOLED, 1B colors,1272 x 2772 pixels
 512GB Storage, 16GB RAM
 Android 16, OxygenOS 16, Qualcomm SM8850-AC Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 (3 nm)
 View deal See latest price on Amazon
 The iQOO Neo 12 is the better gaming phone on paper, as long as iQOO prices it at or below the K100. It wins on the parts that are hardest to fix later, the chip and the cooling. The Redmi K100 is the better buy for one specific person: someone who wants flagship-level speed and cares more about battery life than having the newest processor. Redmi has to name its price first on October 27, and iQOO gets 24 hours to respond. If you’re buying in China, wait until the night of October 28.
 FAQs 
 Is the Snapdragon 8 Elite still good enough for gaming in 2026? 
 Yes. It handles every major mobile game at high settings today, and it powered many of 2025’s flagships. The gap shows up in long sessions and future-proofing
 Do phone cooling fans wear out? 
 A fan is a moving part, so it can wear out or collect dust over time. Brands use sealed air channels and waterproof coatings to reduce the risk.
 Is a cheaper gaming phone good enough for most people? 
 Often, yes. Premium gaming phones add shoulder triggers, faster charging, and more memory, but everyday speed differences are small.
 Which other phones are launching this month? 
 October is packed with launches from Xiaomi, Vivo, OnePlus and Huawei. Our list of October 2026’s biggest phone launches ranks them by whether they’re worth waiting for.
 Do tablets have cooling fans too? 
 Some do. iQOO squeezed a 14,000 RPM fan into an 8.8-inch iQOO Pad Ultra , a sign that active cooling is spreading to devices built for long gaming sessions.
